main_text.p: subire infernales ; Sed juvabit quoque audire Rabbi Isacum Abarbanelem ad Num. cap. 15. vers. 30: Hac de causa venit hæc pœna nomine חמ hoc est, excidii, quod proprie competit ramo, qui exscinditur ab arbore, à qua accipit nutrimentum & vitam, quamdiu ei conjunctus manet: Sic anima exscinditur ex illo fasciculo vitæ superioris, neque recipit splendorem majestatis divinæ, quæ est voluptas & merces animalis. Hæc tamen non est privatio animæ mera, aut destructio totalis: est enim substantia spiritualis, per se subsistens, & natura sua incorruptibilis: Sed חמ sive excidium est pœna & dolor magnus animæ, recipiens magis & minus: & postquam accepit pœnam, recipit etiam oblestationem & voluptatem, sicut dicitur Jobi cap. 14. vers. 7. Est enim deo arbore spes, si præcisa fuerit, & adhuc pullulabit, & propago ejus non deficiet; Pro sententia posteriore pugnant imprimis Rabbi Moses Maimonides, & Rabbi Moses Nachmanides, uti non tantum testatur Rabbi Isac Abarbanel ad Numer cap. 15. vers. 30: Ex quibus vides, quod duo isti Sapientes, Maimonides & Nachamanides, consentiant in excidio animali, quod consistit in privatione animæ, & corruptione vel destructione ejus totalis; tum

page.notes: Hebrew word "חמ" in the text (printed as nmɔ, read as Hebrew נכרת/ נד-ישן ambiguous) and "deo" marks a doubtful reading of a printed "dc" with a hook; the Hebrew abbreviations are approximate. The word "Nachmanides" printed "Mole Nach-" and "Nachamanides" with a Hebrew-letter form; "Isac" is printed "Ifacum" with a doubtful initial. The final word "tum" is a catchword-like continuation at the foot of the text and is kept in the paragraph.
